nary_nodes.label: Bill Oddie dies
evidence: TV presenter and comedian Bill Oddie has died at the age of 85, his agent has said.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event involving deaths or fatalities.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org candidate specifically represents a 'Death' event; 'Event' is the most appropriate parent.

nary_nodes.label: Foster announces Oddie's passing
evidence: In a statement, David Foster said: "It is with deep sadness that I announce the passing of Bill Oddie, the country's best-loved birder."

nary_nodes.label: Humble pays tribute to Oddie
evidence: Paying tribute, Oddie's former Springwatch co-host Kate Humble told BBC Radio 4's The World At One: "No-one could tell a story like Bill. No-one could make me laugh like Bill. No-one could enthuse anyone, whoever they were, to go outside and get excited about a robin."

She added: "Sometimes he'd be fantastically grumpy and would be the last person I'd want to see first thing in the morning, and other times he would just be the best company in the world, and he talked very openly about his struggles with mental health."

nary_nodes.label: Packham pays tribute to Oddie
evidence: Chris Packham, Oddie's successor on Springwatch, wrote on social media: "Sadly we've not only lost a goodie, we've lost one of the besties."

In his tribute, Packham said: "A renegade polymath with binoculars and a beard, Bill was invariably funny and occasionally furious. He loved birds and loathed those who harmed them. He was delightfully unpredictable, sparky, smart and at times a bit spiky."

nary_nodes.label: Idle pays tribute to Oddie
evidence: Python star Eric Idle said he was "very sad" about the loss of Oddie.
"We watched England win the World Cup together at Wembley in '66. He was a very fine songwriter and I learned a lot from him," he wrote on X.

nary_nodes.label: BFI describes Oddie's Goodies role
evidence: Oddie was "known as the hairy, cynical, anarchist member" of the group, the BFI said

nary_nodes.label: West pays tribute to Oddie
evidence: actor and avid birdwatcher Samuel West, who wrote on X about the impact of watching Birding With Bill Oddie.
"Bill Oddie wore a great learning lightly, but he could never hide his enthusiasm," West said.
"His captivated, always improvised narration made that show the platonic ideal of natural history for me, and introduced a whole generation to the fascination of birds."

nary_nodes.label: Moss pays tribute to Oddie
evidence: Naturalist and author Stephen Moss posted that Oddie "did more than anyone to popularise birding".
"Very sad news of the death of Bill Oddie: birder, comedian, musician, artist and environmental campaigner, and dear friend and colleague to me and many others," Moss wrote.

nary_nodes.label: Rowland praises Oddie's impact
evidence: the animal charity's current chief executive Jo Rowland said: "I know many of our wildlife rescuers were inspired into animal welfare by Bill's groundbreaking broadcasting work and incredible knowledge of British birds, which brought the wonders of nature into millions of homes across the country."
"Nature has lost one of its best friends, fiercest champions and most iconic defenders."

nary_nodes.label: Reading FC pays tribute to Oddie
evidence: Reading FC also posted a tribute: "A guest of honour at many matches down the years, he became a much-loved figure at the club."
"Bill's legacy will live on through his iconic chant among Royals supporters at the SCL Stadium and around the country for many years to come."
